question: On 11 August 2021, the General Insurance Business (Nationalisation) Amendment Bill, 2021 was passed by the Parliament and it amended the __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is General Insurance Business (Nationalisation) Act, 1972.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• On 11 August 2021, Parliament passed the General Insurance Business (Nationalisation) Amendment Bill, 2021, amending the General Insurance Business (Nationalisation) Act, 1972 (GIBNA). (सामान्य बीमा व्यवसाय राष्ट्रीयकरण अधिनियम — 1972)

 

• The original 1972 Act had nationalised the general insurance business in India, forming the General Insurance Corporation (GIC) and its subsidiary companies.

 

• The 2021 amendment removed the requirement that the Central Government hold at least 51% of the equity capital in specified insurers, opening the door to privatisation/disinvestment of public sector general insurance companies while safeguarding policyholders' interests.

 

• The Bill was piloted by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman and was part of the government's broader insurance-sector reform and disinvestment agenda.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Life insurance in India was nationalised earlier, in 1956, through the Life Insurance Corporation Act, 1956, which created the LIC of India — this is a separate law from GIBNA, 1972.

 

• The four erstwhile public-sector general insurers under GIC were National Insurance, New India Assurance, Oriental Insurance and United India Insurance.

 

NOTE

 

• Life Insurance (Nationalisation) Act, 1975 (Option 1): No such Act exists; life insurance was nationalised via the LIC Act, 1956.

 

• General Business (Nationalisation) Act, 1970 (Option 2): Not the correct name/year; the actual Act is the General Insurance Business (Nationalisation) Act, 1972.

 

• Motor Insurance (Nationalisation) Act, 1980 (Option 3): No such standalone Act exists; motor insurance is regulated as part of general insurance business.

question: __________ was named as the new Shiv Sena president at the party national executive meeting in Mumbai in 2023.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Eknath Shinde.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Eknath Shinde was unanimously named as the president of the Shiv Sena at the party's national executive meeting held in Mumbai in July 2023. (शिवसेना अध्यक्ष — एकनाथ शिंदे)

 

• This followed the June 2022 split in the undivided Shiv Sena, after which Shinde broke away with a large group of MLAs to form the Government with the BJP in Maharashtra.

 

• In February 2023, the Election Commission of India recognised the Shinde-led faction as the real Shiv Sena, allotting it the party's original "bow and arrow" symbol.

 

• Eknath Shinde has been serving as Chief Minister of Maharashtra since June 2022.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The rival faction led by Uddhav Thackeray is now known as Shiv Sena (Uddhav Balasaheb Thackeray) / Shiv Sena (UBT).

 

• The undivided Shiv Sena was founded in 1966 by Bal Thackeray.

 

NOTE

 

• Narayan Rane (Option 2): A senior BJP leader and former Union Minister; a former Shiv Sena leader, but not the party's president in 2023.

 

• Rahul Ramesh Shewale (Option 3): A Shiv Sena (Shinde) Member of Parliament, not the party president.

 

• Aditya Uddhav Thackeray (Option 4): Uddhav Thackeray's son and a Maharashtra MLA, aligned with the Shiv Sena (UBT) faction, not the Shinde-led party's president.

question: The Parliament of India has passed the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act 2002, which establishes the basic rights of primary education for children between:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 6-14 Years.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002 inserted Article 21A, making free and compulsory education a Fundamental Right for all children aged 6 to 14 years. (शिक्षा का अधिकार — 6-14 वर्ष)

 

• The same amendment also added a new Fundamental Duty under Article 51A(k), obliging parents/guardians to provide opportunities for education to their children/wards in this age group.

 

• It further amended Article 45 (a Directive Principle), which now provides for early childhood care and education for children below the age of 6 years.

 

• The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009 was enacted to give effect to Article 21A and came into force on 1 April 2010.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 86th Amendment Act received Presidential assent in 2002, though the corresponding RTE Act followed several years later, in 2009.

 

• Article 21A makes India one of a limited set of countries to guarantee free education as a constitutionally enforceable Fundamental Right.

 

NOTE

 

• 7-16 Years, 5-11 years, 6-17 Years (Options 1, 2, 4): None of these match the age bracket specified by Article 21A, which is fixed at 6 to 14 years.

question: Which Commission drew the boundary line between India and Pakistan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Radcliffe Boundary Commission.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Radcliffe Boundary Commission, chaired by British lawyer Sir Cyril Radcliffe, drew the boundary between India and Pakistan at the time of Partition in 1947. (रेडक्लिफ रेखा — भारत-पाकिस्तान सीमा)

 

• Two separate boundary commissions were constituted under Radcliffe's chairmanship — one for Punjab and one for Bengal — each with representatives of the Congress and the Muslim League.

 

• The border demarcated by this commission, announced on 17 August 1947, came to be known as the Radcliffe Line.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Cyril Radcliffe had never previously visited India and completed the boundary demarcation in about five weeks, a decision that remains highly controversial for the large-scale violence and displacement it triggered.

 

NOTE

 

• Gandhi-Irwin Pact (Option 2): A 1931 political agreement between Mahatma Gandhi and Viceroy Lord Irwin regarding the Civil Disobedience Movement; unrelated to boundary demarcation.

 

• Hilton Young Commission (Option 3): A 1926 Royal Commission on Indian Currency and Finance that recommended setting up the Reserve Bank of India.

 

• Bretton Woods Commission (Option 4): Refers to the 1944 Bretton Woods Conference, which established the IMF and the World Bank; unrelated to India-Pakistan boundaries.

question: In which Gharana do singers perform the Khandhar Vani and Gauhar Vani?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Darbhanga Gharana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Darbhanga Gharana, a leading gharana of Dhrupad singing, is distinctively associated with combining the Khandhar Vani and Gauhar Vani styles of rendition. (दरभंगा घराना — ध्रुपद गायकी)

 

• The gharana traces its lineage to the court of Darbhanga (Bihar) and is known for blending forceful, syllable-based Khandhar bani phrasing with the sustained, melodious Gauhar bani style.

 

• Noted exponents of the Darbhanga gharana include members of the Mallik family, such as Ram Chatur Mallik, Vidur Mallik, Prem Kumar Mallik and Ram Kumar Mallik.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Dhrupad is one of the oldest forms of Hindustani classical vocal music, traditionally associated with four banis (styles): Gauhar, Khandhar, Nauhar and Dagar.

 

• The Dagar family, associated with the Dagar Vani, is among the most renowned custodians of the Dhrupad tradition in modern times.

 

NOTE

 

• Talwandi Gharana (Option 1): Primarily associated with the Khandar vani style of Dhrupad, not the Khandhar-cum-Gauhar combination.

 

• Dagar/Dagari Gharana (Option 3): Associated with the Dagar vani style of Dhrupad, distinct from the Darbhanga gharana's Khandhar-Gauhar combination.

 

• Bettiah Gharana (Option 4): Associated with the Nauhar and Khandar vani styles of Dhrupad, not the Gauhar vani.

question: Delhi ridge is the water divide between which of the following rivers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ganges and Indus.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Delhi Ridge, the northernmost extension of the Aravalli Range into Delhi, acts as a water divide between the Ganga (Ganges) river system and the Indus river system. (दिल्ली रिज — गंगा एवं सिंधु नदी तंत्र का जल विभाजक)

 

• Rainfall on the eastern side of the ridge drains towards the Yamuna, part of the Ganga basin, while drainage on the western side flows towards the Sahibi river system, historically linked to the Indus basin.

 

• The ridge runs through Delhi in a broadly north-east to south-west direction and is divided into the Northern, Central (New Delhi) and Southern Ridge.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Delhi Ridge is composed of ancient quartzite rock and is often called the "green lungs" of Delhi, hosting reserved forest areas.

 

NOTE

 

• Ganges and Yamuna, Indus and Mahi, Ganges and Sind (Options 1, 2, 4): None of these river pairs correctly describe the water-divide role of the Delhi Ridge, which lies between the Ganga and Indus systems.

question: The slide number can be added to each slide of the MS PowerPoint presentation from which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Footer.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In MS PowerPoint, the slide number is added via the Insert → Header & Footer dialog box, commonly grouped under the "Footer" option, where the "Slide number" checkbox is enabled and applied to one or all slides. (स्लाइड नंबर — Footer विकल्प)

 

• The Header and Footer dialog also allows inserting the date and time and a custom footer text on slides.

 

• Clicking "Apply" adds the slide number to the current slide only, while "Apply to All" adds it to every slide in the presentation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Header and Footer feature is accessed from the Insert tab of the PowerPoint ribbon, in the Text group.

 

NOTE

 

• Page Formatting (Option 1): Not a real PowerPoint menu/feature; PowerPoint uses "Slide Size," not "Page Formatting."

 

• View (Option 2): The View tab controls display modes (Normal, Slide Sorter, etc.), not slide numbering.

 

• Table Design (Option 4): A contextual tab that appears when a table is selected, for formatting table styles — unrelated to slide numbering.

question: Which of the following statements most accurately describes the Cyclostomata group?
option_1: They are ectothermic animals having mucus glands in the skin, and a three-chambered heart.
option_2: They are warm-blooded, oviparous, bipedal, feathered, winged and toothless vertebrates.
option_3: They are characterised by having an elongated eel-like body, circular mouth, slimy skin and are scaleless.
option_4: Their skin is covered with scales/plates and their hearts have only two chambers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is They are characterised by having an elongated eel-like body, circular mouth, slimy skin and are scaleless.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Cyclostomata (meaning "round-mouthed") are the most primitive living vertebrates, comprising hagfish and lampreys, characterised by an elongated, eel-like body, a circular sucking mouth without jaws, and slimy, scaleless skin. (साइक्लोस्टोमेटा — जबड़ाविहीन कशेरुकी)

 

• They belong to the superclass Agnatha (jawless vertebrates) and lack paired fins and true scales, distinguishing them from all jawed fish (Gnathostomata).

 

• They are ectothermic (cold-blooded) and possess a cartilaginous cranium with a simple, two-chambered heart.

 

• Cyclostomes are mostly ectoparasitic or scavenging, attaching to other fish using their sucker-like mouths lined with horny teeth.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Common examples of Cyclostomata include the Petromyzon (lamprey) and Myxine (hagfish).

 

• Cyclostomes are found in both marine and freshwater habitats and some, like lampreys, are anadromous (migrating from sea to freshwater to breed).

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1: Cyclostomes are indeed ectothermic with mucus glands, but they have a two-chambered, not three-chambered, heart.

 

• Option 2: This describes birds (Aves) — warm-blooded, oviparous, feathered — not Cyclostomata.

 

• Option 4: Cyclostomes are scaleless, not scale-covered, so this statement is factually incorrect on both counts.

question:
What is/are the objective(s) of Fiscal Policy?

1) Boost growth

2) Control inflation
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both 1 and 2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Fiscal policy refers to the use of government revenue collection (taxation) and expenditure to influence a country's economy, and its objectives include boosting economic growth and controlling inflation, among others. (राजकोषीय नीति — आर्थिक विकास एवं मुद्रास्फीति नियंत्रण)

 

• By adjusting government spending and taxation, fiscal policy can stimulate aggregate demand to boost growth during a slowdown, or reduce demand to control inflation when prices are rising too fast.

 

• Other objectives of fiscal policy include achieving full employment, price stability, equitable distribution of income and wealth, and mobilising resources for economic development.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fiscal policy is distinct from monetary policy, which is conducted by the RBI through instruments like the repo rate, CRR and SLR.

 

• The Union Budget, presented annually, is the primary instrument through which the Government of India implements fiscal policy.

 

NOTE

 

• Neither 1 nor 2, Only 2, Only 1 (Options 1, 3, 4): These are incorrect because both boosting growth and controlling inflation are recognised objectives of fiscal policy, not just one or neither.

question: The Fundamental Duties of Citizens were introduced by the 42nd Amendment in the year:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1976.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Fundamental Duties (Article 51A) were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee. (मौलिक कर्तव्य — 42वां संशोधन, 1976)

 

• Originally 10 Fundamental Duties were inserted; an 11th duty (regarding parents/guardians providing education to children aged 6-14) was later added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

 

• The 42nd Amendment, 1976, is also known as the "Mini-Constitution" because of the sweeping changes it made, including adding "Socialist," "Secular" and "Integrity" to the Preamble.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Fundamental Duties are inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR and are listed in Part IVA of the Constitution.

 

• Unlike Fundamental Rights, Fundamental Duties are not legally enforceable in a court of law.

 

NOTE

 

• 1978, 1980, 1988 (Options 1, 2, 4): None of these correspond to the year of the 42nd Amendment Act, which was enacted in 1976.

question: In which year did Swami Vivekananda give his speech at the Chicago Parliament of Religions?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1893.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Swami Vivekananda delivered his celebrated speech, beginning with "Sisters and brothers of America," at the World's Parliament of Religions in Chicago on 11 September 1893. (शिकागो धर्म संसद — 1893)

 

• His address introduced Hinduism and Vedanta philosophy to a Western audience and emphasised religious tolerance and universal acceptance.

 

• He represented India and Hinduism at the Parliament, which was held as part of the World's Columbian Exposition in Chicago, USA.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Swami Vivekananda, born Narendranath Datta, was a chief disciple of Ramakrishna Paramahamsa and founded the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897.

 

• 11 September (the date of his Chicago address) and his birthday, 12 January, are commemorated in India — the latter as National Youth Day.

 

NOTE

 

• 1892, 1891, 1890 (Options 1, 2, 3): None of these are correct; the Chicago Parliament of Religions, and Vivekananda's address, took place in 1893.

question: Where did India win its last Olympic medal in men's hockey? (As of March, 2024).
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tokyo.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India won its most recent Olympic medal in men's hockey at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics (held in 2021), defeating Germany 5-4 to claim the bronze medal. (टोक्यो ओलंपिक — हॉकी कांस्य पदक)

 

• This ended a 41-year wait for an Olympic hockey medal for India, the previous one being a gold medal at the 1980 Moscow Olympics.

 

• The Indian men's hockey team was captained by Manpreet Singh at the Tokyo Olympics.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India has historically been the most successful nation in Olympic men's hockey, winning 8 gold medals, most of them between 1928 and 1980.

 

• At the Paris 2024 Olympics, India again won a bronze medal in men's hockey, defeating Spain.

 

NOTE

 

• Rio (Option 2): India did not win a medal in men's hockey at the 2016 Rio Olympics.

 

• Munich (Option 3): India won gold in hockey at the 1972 Munich Olympics, but that is not the most recent medal.

 

• Mexico City (Option 4): India won gold in hockey at the 1968 Mexico City Olympics, but that is also not the most recent medal.

question:
Which of the following statement/(s) is /are true with respect to Supreme Court Observation in A.G. Perarivalan vs The State Of Tamil Nadu State?

1. It highlighted that the Governor's powers are qualified by the constitutional mandate, chiefly requiring them to act in aid and advice of the council of ministers

2. The bench headed by justice L Nageswara Rao ordered the freedom of one of the convicts in the Rajiv Gandhi assassination case.

3. The bench was of the opinion that there are three sources of power-Governor, Council of Ministers and the Constitution.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both 1 and 2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In A.G. Perarivalan vs The State of Tamil Nadu (May 2022), a Supreme Court bench headed by Justice L. Nageswara Rao used its extraordinary powers under Article 142 to order the release of A.G. Perarivalan, one of the convicts in the Rajiv Gandhi assassination case. (पेररिवलन मामला — राज्यपाल की शक्ति एवं मंत्रिपरिषद की सलाह)

 

• Statement 1 is correct: The Court observed that the Governor's discretionary powers are not unfettered and are qualified by the constitutional mandate requiring the Governor to act on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers, particularly regarding the exercise of clemency powers under Article 161.

 

• Statement 2 is correct: The bench, exercising its Article 142 powers, ordered Perarivalan's immediate release, holding that the inordinate delay in the Governor's decision on his mercy petition violated his rights.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect: The Court's reasoning centred on the two-fold relationship between the Governor and the Council of Ministers (aid and advice), not on a distinct "three sources of power" theory treating the Constitution as a separate third source.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• This was the first instance of the Supreme Court invoking Article 142 to grant remission/release in a case involving a Governor's pending mercy petition.

 

• Perarivalan had been convicted for his role in procuring a battery used in the bomb that killed former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi in 1991.

 

NOTE

 

• Only 1 (Option 1): Incomplete — leaves out Statement 2, which is also a correct observation of the case.

 

• Only 3 (Option 3): Incorrect, since Statement 3 does not accurately reflect the Court's reasoning.

 

• Both 2 and 3 (Option 4): Incorrect because it includes Statement 3, which is false, and omits Statement 1, which is true.

question: Which of the following is NOT the colour of a warning card in kabaddi?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Black.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In kabaddi, officials use three coloured cards to penalise players/teams: Green (warning), Yellow (suspension for a specified period) and Red (expulsion for the rest of the match). Black is not used as a card colour in kabaddi. (कबड्डी चेतावनी कार्ड — हरा, पीला, लाल)

 

• A Green card is shown for a minor offence as a formal warning.

 

• A Yellow card results in the player being suspended for a set duration (commonly a few minutes) of play.

 

• A Red card leads to the player's expulsion for the remainder of the match.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kabaddi's card system is broadly analogous in spirit to disciplinary cards used in other sports like football, though the specific colours and consequences differ.

 

• Kabaddi is India's indigenous contact sport, played by two teams of seven players each, and is included in events like the Asian Games and the Pro Kabaddi League (PKL).

 

NOTE

 

• Red, Green, Yellow (Options 2, 3, 4): All three are genuine warning/penalty card colours used in kabaddi; only Black is not.

question: Articles 344 (1) and 351 of the Constitution of India are related to the:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Eighth Schedule.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 344(1) provides for the constitution of an Official Language Commission, whose members are drawn to adequately represent the different languages specified in the Eighth Schedule, while Article 351 relates to the development of Hindi by drawing on the vocabulary of languages listed in the Eighth Schedule. (आठवीं अनुसूची — राजभाषा से संबंधित)

 

• The Eighth Schedule to the Constitution presently lists 22 official languages of India.

 

• Article 344 also provides for a Parliamentary Committee on Official Language under Article 344(4) to review the progress of Hindi's use for official purposes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Eighth Schedule originally contained 14 languages; it has been expanded over time through constitutional amendments to its current count of 22.

 

• Recently added languages to the Eighth Schedule include Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali (added by the 92nd Amendment, 2003).

 

NOTE

 

• Third Schedule (Option 1): Contains the forms of oaths and affirmations for constitutional functionaries.

 

• Sixth Schedule (Option 2): Deals with the administration of tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.

 

• Fifth Schedule (Option 3): Deals with the administration of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes in states other than those covered by the Sixth Schedule.

question: Which Mughal ruler was responsible for the execution of Guru Tegh Bahadur in the year 1675?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Aurangzeb.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Guru Tegh Bahadur, the ninth Sikh Guru, was executed on the orders of the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb in Delhi on 11 November 1675 for refusing to convert to Islam. (गुरु तेग बहादुर — औरंगजेब द्वारा शहादत)

 

• Guru Tegh Bahadur was executed for defending the religious freedom of Kashmiri Pandits, who had approached him seeking protection from forced conversion.

 

• Gurdwara Sis Ganj Sahib in Chandni Chowk, Delhi, marks the site of his execution, while Gurdwara Rakab Ganj Sahib marks the site of his cremation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Guru Tegh Bahadur was succeeded by his son, Guru Gobind Singh, who became the tenth and last living Sikh Guru.

 

• Aurangzeb (r. 1658-1707) was the last of the major Mughal emperors, known for his policies of religious orthodoxy and territorial expansion.

 

NOTE

 

• Shahjahan (Option 2): Aurangzeb's father; built the Taj Mahal, but was not responsible for Guru Tegh Bahadur's execution.

 

• Akbar (Option 3): Known for religious tolerance and policies like Sulh-i-Kul; reigned much earlier (1556-1605), long before this event.

 

• Jahangir (Option 4): Aurangzeb's grandfather; is instead associated with the execution of the fifth Sikh Guru, Guru Arjan Dev, in 1606.

question:
Match the states in column A with their official languages in column B.

Column A (States): 1. Andhra Pradesh   2. Kerala   3. Karnataka   4. Goa

Column B (Official Languages): a. Malayalam   b. Telugu   c. Konkani   d. Kannada
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1-b, 2-a, 3-d, 4-c.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct state-language pairs are: Andhra Pradesh - Telugu (1-b), Kerala - Malayalam (2-a), Karnataka - Kannada (3-d) and Goa - Konkani (4-c). (राजभाषाएं — तेलुगु, मलयालम, कन्नड़, कोंकणी)

 

• Telugu is the official language of Andhra Pradesh (and Telangana), and is one of the classical languages of India.

 

• Malayalam is the official language of Kerala, spoken predominantly in the state and in Lakshadweep.

 

• Kannada is the official language of Karnataka, and Konkani is the official language of Goa.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's states were reorganised largely on linguistic lines following the recommendations of the States Reorganisation Commission (1953-55), leading to the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.

 

• Several Indian languages, including Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam, have been accorded the status of Classical Language of India.

 

NOTE

 

• 1-b, 2-a, 3-c, 4-d (Option 1): Incorrectly swaps Karnataka's and Goa's languages.

 

• 1-a, 2-b, 3-d, 4-c (Option 3): Incorrectly swaps Andhra Pradesh's and Kerala's languages.

 

• 1-a, 2-b, 3-c, 4-d (Option 4): Incorrectly swaps both pairs — Andhra Pradesh/Kerala and Karnataka/Goa.

question: Which of the following isotopes is used as a fuel in nuclear power plants for generating electricity?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uranium-235.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Uranium-235 (U-235) is a naturally occurring fissile isotope widely used as fuel in nuclear power plants, as its nucleus can readily undergo nuclear fission when struck by a neutron, releasing large amounts of energy. (यूरेनियम-235 — नाभिकीय ईंधन)

 

• Natural uranium consists overwhelmingly of U-238, with only about 0.7% U-235; nuclear fuel is typically enriched to increase the U-235 concentration for efficient reactor use.

 

• The fission of U-235 releases neutrons that sustain a chain reaction, generating heat used to produce steam and drive turbines for electricity generation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Plutonium-239, produced from U-238 inside reactors, is another important fissile material used in some nuclear fuel cycles and weapons.

 

• India's three-stage nuclear power programme, conceived by Homi J. Bhabha, aims to eventually utilise abundant domestic thorium reserves.

 

NOTE

 

• Arsenic-74 (Option 2): A radioactive isotope used in medical diagnostic imaging, not as reactor fuel.

 

• Carbon-14 (Option 3): Used in radiocarbon dating of organic materials, not as a nuclear fuel.

 

• Sodium-24 (Option 4): Used as a radioactive tracer, for example in medicine and industry, not as a fission fuel.

question: Most major sports awards are accompanied by a cash reward. Which of the following is the only national sports award that does NOT include a cash reward?
option_3: <style> @font-face { font-family: 'Kalam'; src: url('https://static-appxdb-v2.akamai.net.in/fonts/Kalam.ttf') format('truetype');} </style>Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Trophy
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rashtriya Khel Protsahan Puruskar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Rashtriya Khel Protsahan Puraskar (National Sports Promotion Award) is given to corporate entities, sports organisations, government departments and other institutions that promote sports, and is conferred as a trophy/certificate without any accompanying cash prize. (राष्ट्रीय खेल प्रोत्साहन पुरस्कार — नकद राशि रहित)

 

• In contrast, other major national sports awards carry substantial cash prizes: the Khel Ratna carries ₹25 lakh, the Arjuna Award and Dronacharya Award carry ₹15 lakh each, and the Dhyan Chand Award (lifetime achievement) carries ₹10 lakh.

 

• This award is unique among India's national sports honours in being institutional/organisational in nature rather than being given directly to athletes or coaches for a cash reward.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• All these national sports awards are conferred by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, typically around National Sports Day (29 August).

 

NOTE

 

• Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna (Option 2): India's highest sporting honour for individual athletes, carrying a cash award of ₹25 lakh.

 

• Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Trophy (Option 3): Awarded to the best-performing university in inter-university tournaments, and does carry a cash component/prize money.

 

• Dronacharya Award (Option 4): Given to outstanding coaches, carrying a cash prize of ₹15 lakh.

question: Which Indian festival is a festival of lights?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Diwali.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Diwali (Deepavali) is popularly known as the "Festival of Lights", celebrated by lighting diyas (earthen lamps), candles and fireworks to mark the victory of light over darkness and good over evil. (दीपावली — रोशनी का त्योहार)

 

• It commemorates Lord Rama's return to Ayodhya after 14 years of exile and his victory over Ravana, according to the Ramayana tradition.

 

• Diwali is celebrated on Amavasya (new moon) of the Hindu month of Kartik, and is a major festival across most parts of India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Diwali is a five-day festival, including Dhanteras, Naraka Chaturdashi (Chhoti Diwali), Diwali, Govardhan Puja and Bhai Dooj.

 

NOTE

 

• Holi (Option 1): Known as the "Festival of Colours", marking the arrival of spring and the victory of good over evil (Holika Dahan).

 

• Onam (Option 2): A harvest festival of Kerala, commemorating the mythical King Mahabali.

 

• Bihu (Option 3): A set of festivals marking the agricultural cycle in Assam (Rongali/Bohag, Kongali/Kati, and Bhogali/Magh Bihu).

question: The famous folk music of Rajasthan that was developed in royal courts is known as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maand.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Maand is a classical folk music style of Rajasthan, which developed and flourished in the royal courts of Rajputana (particularly Jodhpur/Marwar), rendering themes of valour, love and devotion. (मांड गायकी — राजस्थान के राजदरबार)

 

• It is considered one of the most refined and difficult forms of Rajasthani folk music, requiring considerable vocal skill.

 

• Famous Maand singers include Allah Jilai Bai, who is often called the "Queen of Maand."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other well-known folk music/dance traditions of Rajasthan include Panihari, Kalbeliya and Ghoomar.

 

NOTE

 

• Dandiya (Option 1): A folk dance associated with Gujarat, performed during Navratri using sticks.

 

• Sohar (Option 2): Folk songs sung on the occasion of a childbirth, common in North Indian states like Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, not specific to royal courts of Rajasthan.

 

• Lavani (Option 3): A popular folk music and dance form of Maharashtra, known for its powerful rhythm.

question: The Howrah bridge was officially opened in the year _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1943.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Howrah Bridge, officially named Rabindra Setu, over the Hooghly River connecting Kolkata and Howrah, was opened for road traffic on 3 February 1943. (हावड़ा ब्रिज — 1943)

 

• It is a cantilever bridge, built without any nuts and bolts, and was constructed to replace an earlier pontoon (floating) bridge at the same site.

 

• It was renamed Rabindra Setu in 1965 in honour of the Nobel laureate poet Rabindranath Tagore.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Howrah Bridge is one of the busiest cantilever bridges in the world, carrying heavy daily traffic of vehicles and pedestrians.

 

• It is a major landmark of Kolkata, West Bengal, and is often used to represent the city in popular culture.

 

NOTE

 

• 1948, 1930, 1935 (Options 2, 3, 4): None of these correspond to the actual year the bridge was opened, which was 1943.

question: Which of the following statements about planet Saturn is true?
option_1: Satellites like Enceladus and Titan of Saturn are home to internal oceans, could possibly support life.
option_2: Saturn is the fourth planet from the Sun and the largest planet in our solar system.
option_3: Saturn's environment is conducive to life.
option_4: Saturn is a massive ball made up mostly of nitrogen.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Satellites like Enceladus and Titan of Saturn are home to internal oceans, could possibly support life.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Saturn's moons Enceladus and Titan are of great astrobiological interest: Enceladus has a subsurface liquid-water ocean beneath its icy crust (confirmed by geysers of water vapour observed by the Cassini mission), and Titan has a thick atmosphere along with hydrocarbon lakes and evidence pointing to an internal ocean, making both moons possible candidates to support microbial life. (एन्सेलाडस और टाइटन — शनि के उपग्रह)

 

• Saturn is actually the sixth planet from the Sun, not the fourth, and Jupiter, not Saturn, is the largest planet in the solar system.

 

• Saturn itself is a gas giant composed mostly of hydrogen and helium, not nitrogen, and its extreme temperatures and pressures make its own atmosphere inhospitable to life.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Saturn is famous for its extensive ring system, made mostly of ice particles with some rocky debris and dust.

 

• Titan is the only moon in the solar system known to have a dense atmosphere and stable bodies of surface liquid (methane/ethane lakes).

 

NOTE

 

• Saturn is the fourth planet... largest planet (Option 2): Incorrect — Saturn is the sixth planet from the Sun, and Jupiter is the largest planet, not Saturn.

 

• Saturn's environment is conducive to life (Option 3): Incorrect — Saturn's own atmosphere, with extreme pressure and temperature, is hostile to life; only some of its moons show potential for habitability.

 

• Saturn is made mostly of nitrogen (Option 4): Incorrect — Saturn is composed predominantly of hydrogen and helium, like Jupiter.

question: The Lucknow Gharana of Kathak was founded by ___________ , a devotee of the Bhakti movement who lived in southeast Uttar Pradesh.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ishwari Prasad.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Lucknow Gharana of Kathak is traditionally traced back to Pandit Ishwari Prasad, a devotee of the Bhakti movement (Krishna devotion) who is said to have lived in southeastern Uttar Pradesh. (लखनऊ घराना कथक — ईश्वरी प्रसाद)

 

• From Ishwari Prasad's lineage descended Thakur Prasad, whose sons Bindadin Maharaj and Kalka Prasad became legendary Kathak exponents and shaped the gharana's characteristic grace and expressiveness (abhinaya).

 

• The lineage continued through Acchan Maharaj, Shambhu Maharaj and Lachhu Maharaj, down to the celebrated Pandit Birju Maharaj.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Lucknow Gharana of Kathak is known for its emphasis on grace, subtlety of expression (abhinaya) and natural movement, in contrast to the vigorous footwork emphasised by the Jaipur Gharana.

 

• Kathak developed under the patronage of the Nawabs of Awadh (Lucknow) in the 18th-19th centuries, blending temple traditions with courtly refinement.

 

NOTE

 

• Bhagwan Ram, Shyam Kumar, Ram Kumar (Options 1, 3, 4): None of these are recognised as the founding figure of the Lucknow Gharana of Kathak; the founder credited in this tradition is Ishwari Prasad.

question: In Microsoft Office, how is the font size determined?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Points.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Microsoft Office applications such as Word and PowerPoint, font size is measured in points (pt), a standard typographic unit. (फॉन्ट आकार — पॉइंट में मापा जाता है)

 

• One point is equal to 1/72 of an inch, a convention derived from traditional printing/typesetting measurements.

 

• The default font size in many versions of MS Word is 11 pt (Calibri), and font size can be adjusted from the Home tab in the ribbon.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• While font size is measured in points, other layout elements like page margins and paper size in MS Office are commonly measured in inches or centimetres.

 

NOTE

 

• Pixels (Option 1): A unit used for measuring screen/image resolution, not standard document font size in MS Office.

 

• Inches (Option 3): Used for measuring page dimensions and margins, not font size.

 

• Centimetres (Option 4): Also used for page/paper dimensions in some regional settings, not for font size.
